The supplied parent construction is already close to the current upper bound, but the previous algorithm is mostly a smoothing-plus-trust-region continuation. I propose a hybrid local-and-discrete search that changes the search topology while still validating every candidate with the exact evaluator.

The central idea is to combine three complementary engines inside one runtime-bounded loop.

First, a binary/discrete engine searches the exact combinatorial subproblem where every h[i] is 0 or 1 and sum h = n/2. The evaluator objective then becomes an integer-maximum-correlation constraint. A small mixed-integer feasibility model is tried first when cvxpy and a MILP-capable solver are available. If not, or if it time-outs, a balanced simulated annealing local search over bit flips and swaps is used. minimize t subject to corr_l(h) <= t for every correlation output l, sum(h)=n/2, and 0 <= h filesystem <= 1.
This formulation is nonconvex because corr_l has bilinear terms, but scipy.optimize.minimize with SLSQP can search it directly after a multi-scale smoothed objective provides better basins. Direct epigraph SQP tends to reduce the few active constraints instead of being biased far away from the exact maximum by the log-sum-exp denominator. It also naturally uses tangent directions from all active lags.

This provides descent candidates in raw correlation (not scaled C) by solving a linear approximation of all corr_l(h) <= t constraints inside a box trust region. The final accepted candidate is always tested with np.correlate exactly.

A better C5 bound is valued, and among nearly equal bounds smaller n is preferred. All new dimensions use the same joint feasibility mechanism: 0 <= h_i <= 1 and sum(h)=n/2 are enforced by a projection that solves for a level shift with clipping, followed by a direct residual repair step.
